Anyone interested in simply arming up, rather than crafting from scratch, it's very easy to assemble a couple of premade segments into a functional rifle, and it doesn't cost very much either.

First, you have the "Lower." This is the serialized part that the ATF considers a gun, so it's what has to be shipped to a dealer and transferred to you.

This is one of the least expensive lowers you're going to find, and I can vouch for PSA's quality. I'm rough on equipment and their lowers have held up wonderfully in my care. These were $10 cheaper around the holidays on sale, so they CAN go cheaper, but they start at $130 for the basic, bog standard platform https://palmettostatearmory.com/complete-psa-ar-15-lower-classic-edition.html

Personally, I'm not a fan of the M4 stock. On my carbine, I went with a fancier, more comfortable stock for $150. https://palmettostatearmory.com/psa-ar-15-complete-lower-magpul-moe-edition-black-no-magazine-7065.html

Or, if you prefer the older school approach, they have some nice Fixed Stock lowers like I used for my Rifle Length build for $170 https://palmettostatearmory.com/psa-complete-rifle-lower-receiver-a2.html

Next, you need an Upper to mate to the lower. This can ship directly to you.

16" is the shortest you can go for barrel length without a tax stamp or using a pistol build. But Barrel Length is good, 16" to 20" is where you want to be anyway, if you ask me.

This one is a fairly standard upper build, no fancy rails, fixed front sight, and it comes with its own bolt carrier (this is what pushes bullets into place and makes them fire) and charging handle (You pull back on this to make the rifle ready to fire). Some uppers come with those parts, others do not. Be careful when shopping around. This is $220, so if you combined this with your $130 Basic Lower, that's a total of $350 for a near complete rifle. https://palmettostatearmory.com/psa-classic-freedom-m4-upper-with-bcg-and-ch.html

This upper, from Bear Creek, would pair well with that fixed stock PSA Lower, for a M16 style build. It too comes with the Bolt Carrier and Charging handle, for $250. https://www.bearcreekarsenal.com/5-56-nato-20-black-nitride-heavy-barrel-1-9-twist-rifle-length-gas-system-rifle-handguard-a2-front-sight-carry-handle-upper

Here's one without the fixed-front-sight, a 16" barrel, with mlok handguards (Basically these handguards have slots to fasten attachments to). from BCA: for $190. https://www.bearcreekarsenal.com/bca-ar-15-complete-upper-assembly-10-5-parkerized-4150-contour-barrel-5-56-nato-1-7-twist-w-10-m-lok-rail

Some of these will need rear sights, which run $20+ for a UTG flip-up Rear sight or $30+ for a Carry Handle rear sight. $20 and up will also get you a flip up front sight from UTG. Magpul makes nice flip up sights as well, but cost more than twice what the UTG sights do. You'll want to start with Three to Five magazines, and there's no such thing as too many magazines. Aluminum 30rd magazines are usually around $8 to $10 apiece, whereas polymer 30 rd mags usually go for around twice that. There are 10, 20 and 40 round options out there as well. Beyond that you start talking about specialty devices and reliability usually decreases.
